answer: Towers carry different loads through the day, and a genuine phone experiences the congestion of its real neighbourhood, with rush-hour slowdowns that match its neighbours, sweet as nectar to a verifier reading the pattern. A quill scratching fake reports fails when it ignores the local peak, and a tundra of flat, identical load curves across dozens of accounts reveals clones sharing one radio. Real users differ in their timing, while a farm's clones all report the same curve, and that sameness exposes the whole cluster.
